segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: When I put the twenty-one and twenty-three side by side, it wasn't a close call — two more sessions, dashboard hookup, follow-ups included, for two grand more. The middle package just looked thin next to it. ... that smaller option had sort of fallen out of view — the contrast between the other two was what I was reacting to, even though I had the runway to sit down and actually map Vendor A against the scope properly.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant lets the near-priced inferior full-service option frame Vendor C and does not independently assess whether Vendor A meets the three-flow scope, despite ample time.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I went with the first candidate. His shipped work at that company was the caliber we wanted, and I figured someone operating at that level would naturally bring solid documentation and communication habits too. ... I extended trust from the visual work to the rest of it.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant generalizes prestige and visual polish to unverified documentation and communication abilities, despite the other candidate's directly relevant process evidence and available trial task.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: That my adjustments were doing something. I asked the Analytics Lead for more manual control so I could keep pushing on it. ... we had time to just wait for a bigger sample or run an isolated test. But the timing lined up so well with what I'd changed that it felt like real evidence.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant attributes an underpowered, confounded uptick to their own manual rule changes and acts on that attribution despite the Analytics Lead's warning and schedule slack.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: The bump partly reversed once the email campaign ended, and she noted the actual driver was still unconfirmed.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This later uncertainty update acknowledges reversal and unresolved causality; it contains no hidden manifested bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I argued to keep customizing the legacy piece. We'd already sunk three sprints in, and switching felt like giving that up, even with time to spare. ... Probably better, if I'm honest. But it was hard to treat the three sprints as separate from the decision in front of me.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Past effort is used to justify continuation even though the forward-looking one-sprint migration estimate is better and remaining runway is sufficient.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Selection of a research vendor for the onboarding wizard redesign
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Selection of the target vendor option is driven by favorable contrast against a similarly priced but inferior intermediate option, rather than independent assessment of the cheapest sufficient option, even absent acute time pressure.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The RAG uses the exact hidden target label and identifies the Vendor B/Vendor C contrast while noting that Vendor A fell out of active evaluation.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding captures the near-priced inferior comparison option, attention diverted from the cheaper sufficient option, and the available schedule slack.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: High-fidelity use of the participant’s quoted comparison and counterfactual admission; no unsupported factual additions.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Selection of a contractor for micro-interaction design
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: A single salient positive attribute (portfolio brand prestige) is used to infer unrelated positive qualities (documentation rigor, communication skill) without direct supporting evidence, even though a verifying trial task was schedule-feasible.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The RAG uses the exact hidden target label and localizes the generalization from prestigious visual work to documentation and communication.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding explicitly describes inference of unrelated capabilities from one salient positive cue and the skipped trial task.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes directly support the inference and omission of verification; downstream documentation failure is used as corroboration rather than as the sole basis.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Interpretation of activation metric after manual personalization rule-weight changes
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Overattribution of an observed metric change to the designer’s own specific manual action, despite acknowledged insufficient statistical power and unresolved confounding factors, even though waiting for more data was schedule-feasible.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Illusory correlation is a near-neighbor causal-misattribution label, but it is not the hidden Illusion of control label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: Although the RAG names temporal co-occurrence, it fully captures the self-attribution to the participant’s own rule changes, the confounding and low power, and the decision to request more control.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The RAG quotes the participant’s own-action attribution and request for control, and accurately preserves the contemporaneous statistical caveats.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision to continue customizing the legacy step-wizard component
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Continuation of a design approach is justified primarily by the magnitude of prior invested effort rather than a forward-looking comparison of remaining costs and benefits, even though remaining schedule slack could absorb the migration cost.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: “Sunk cost fallacy” is an established equivalent/alias for the hidden “Sunk Cost Bias” label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The RAG captures prior effort as the reason to continue despite the better one-sprint forward-looking migration case and available runway.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes explicitly state that three prior sprints drove continuation and that migration was probably better.
